Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

text:
This looks like a crisis snapshot with the policy rate at a very low z-score, VIX and credit spreads at maximum, and equities crashing. Two episodes fit: late 2008 and March 2020.

March 2020 fits several details. The fed funds rate fell 3 z-scores in 3 months, from 1.5% to near 0, which fits a 36-month window where rates had been high. The 10-year yield z-score of -3 also fits. Unemployment at -1.5 z fits because it was still low (March 2020 was 4.4%), and payrolls average +1.5 fits too. Core CPI at +1.5 fits as well. Industrial production at -1.5 fits, since it was weak in 2019. The dollar at +1.5 with a +2.0 3-month change fits the March 2020 dollar spike. Investment-grade credit at -3 for 1 month fits March 2020, when it fell sharply. Gold at -0.5 for 1 month also fits March 2020, when it dipped.

Late 2008 fits less well. Unemployment was rising then, payrolls were deeply negative, and the Treasury rally came with credit collapse. The payroll figure of +1.5 rules out 2008.

So the snapshot is March 2020.
